mechanism_narrative: Continued improvement in RETAIL_REC, TRANSIT, and WORKPLACES mobility over the past three weeks signals a sustained reopening trend that will lift retail footfall further, causing RETAIL_REC to be higher over the next four weeks than over the last four weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is not higher than over the last 28 days despite continued improvement in RETAIL_REC, TRANSIT, and WORKPLACES.

mechanism_narrative: When TRANSIT mobility crosses above -70 percent (i.e., becomes less negative than -70), it indicates that travel restrictions have eased enough to spur retail activity, so RETAIL_REC will rise over the next two weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not increase in the two weeks following a TRANSIT crossing above -70.

mechanism_narrative: The interaction of rising WORKPLACES mobility (less negative) and falling RESIDENTIAL mobility (less positive) indicates more people leaving home for work and leisure, which jointly boosts retail footfall, leading to higher RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not rise when WORKPLACES increases and RESIDENTIAL decreases simultaneously.

mechanism_narrative: In a reopening regime, improvement in GROCERY_PHARM mobility (less negative) reflects a return to normal shopping habits, which spills over to retail, causing RETAIL_REC to increase over the next week.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC falls or stays flat in the week following an improvement in GROCERY_PHARM mobility.

mechanism_narrative: Rising PARKS mobility indicates increased outdoor leisure activity, which is associated with higher foot traffic in retail areas, so RETAIL_REC will be higher over the next two weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not increase when PARKS mobility rises.

mechanism_narrative: When RESIDENTIAL mobility falls below 20 percent above baseline (i.e., less than 20), it signals that more people are leaving home, which drives retail activity, leading to higher RETAIL_REC over the next two weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not increase after RESIDENTIAL falls below 20.

mechanism_narrative: The interaction between rising PARKS mobility and RETAIL_REC recovery suggests favorable seasonal conditions (e.g., spring) that simultaneously boost outdoor and retail activity, so RETAIL_REC will continue to rise over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not increase when PARKS mobility rises during the seasonal period.

mechanism_narrative: If RESIDENTIAL mobility remains above 20 percent above baseline, it indicates continued elevated stay-at-home behavior that limits retail footfall, causing RETAIL_REC to be lower over the next four weeks than over the last four weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC increases over the next four weeks despite RESIDENTIAL remaining above 20.
